title: Dengue surge overwhelms Dili health centres; 609 cases in January
detail: Dili Municipal Health Service reported 386 new dengue cases in a week and 609 in January with two deaths; Comoro Health Centre had to transfer patients to Formosa, and severe cases went to Guido Valadares National Hospital.

title: Eight-hour blackout in Oecusse after Sakato power plant fault
detail: EDTL said a failed fuse cut-out on feeder 02 at the Sakato plant blacked out customers from Numbei to Lifau from about 02:40 to 11:00.

title: PNTL searches Dili homes in counterfeit US dollar probe
detail: PNTL criminal investigators searched homes in Fatuhada and Becora linked to two suspects, seizing laptops, phones and bank details; it follows the 16 April arrest of three people accused of making fake currency at a Bidau warehouse.

title: Rain-triggered landslide forces 15 families out near Turiscai
detail: Heavy rain triggered a landslide around 04:00 that destroyed crops and blocked a road under rehabilitation; local administrators said 15 families were moved to temporary shelter and Civil Protection teams were monitoring. No casualties reported.

title: Bobonaro police log 42 road crashes and 3 deaths Jan-May
detail: PNTL Bobonaro recorded 42 traffic accidents from January to May 2026, three fatal, and blamed mostly human factors such as ignoring signals and not wearing helmets.

title: PNTL raids three Dili scam compounds; 253 workers arrested
detail: National Police raided three secured call-centre compounds in Dili over five days, arresting 253 mostly Chinese and Indonesian workers plus Cambodians and seizing laptops, SIM cards and Starlink units; 314 held since late June, facing money-laundering, criminal-association and illegal-gaming charges. Over 50 had no passports.

title: Scam-centre arrests pass 350 incl. 61 held at Tibar
detail: Fundasaun Mahein reported over 350 people, mainly Chinese and Indonesian nationals, arrested by PNTL and PCIC in raids in Dili, Liquiçá and Tibar by 20 July, including 61 foreigners at one Tibar site; the government suspended proposed iGaming licences and some detainees were released after judicial review.

title: UNODC flags Timor-Leste and Oecusse as highly vulnerable to scam networks
detail: A UNODC report named Timor-Leste among the countries most vulnerable to transnational cybercrime expansion and flagged the Oé-Cusse special region and its Digital Centre as at risk of hosting scam compounds displaced from neighbouring countries.

title: Ministry of Health: 4,000 dengue cases and 32 deaths Jan-July
detail: The Ministry of Health reported about 4,000 dengue cases and 32 deaths in the first seven months of 2026, highest in Dili's Dom Aleixo and Cristo Rei posts, with children under 14 most affected.

title: Timor-Leste and Indonesia meet on two unresolved land border segments
detail: Delegations met in Jakarta on the Noel Besi-Citrana-Naktuka and Bidjael Sunan-Oben segments, agreeing to use uti possidetis juris and the 1904 Treaty as references, and discussed a cross-border irrigation project in Bobonaro.

title: Civil Protection to relocate 57 erosion-hit families in Ila, Covalima
detail: The Civil Protection Authority said it will move 57 families affected by land erosion in Ila village, Maucatar post, to a new neighbourhood, with building materials prepared by the government.
